chapters.title: Naomi and Ruth
chapters.html:
Ruth 1

Moab

1And it came to pass in the days when the judges ruled that there was a famine in the land, and a man of Bethlehem in Judah went to live as a guest in the country of Moab, he and his wife and his two sons.

2The man's name was Elimelech, his wife's name was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They came into the country of Moab and stayed there.

3Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons.

4They took Moabite wives for themselves; the name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the other Ruth. They lived there about ten years.

5Then both Mahlon and Chilion also died, and the woman was left without her two children and without her husband.

The Road Back

6She rose with her daughters-in-law to return from the country of Moab, for she had heard in the country of Moab that the LORD had visited His people and given them bread.

7She went out from the place where she had been, and her two daughters-in-law with her, and they set out on the way to return to the land of Judah.

8Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, "Go, return each of you to her mother's house. May the LORD show you loyal love, as you have shown it to the dead and to me.

9May the LORD grant that you find rest, each of you in the house of her husband." Then she kissed them, and they lifted up their voices and wept.

10They said to her, "No, we will return with you to your people."

11But Naomi said, "Turn back, my daughters. Why will you go with me? Have I still sons in my womb who could become your husbands?

12Turn back, my daughters, go; for I am too old to have a husband. If I said, 'I have hope,' even if I had a husband tonight and should also bear sons,

13would you wait for them until they were grown? Would you hold yourselves back from having husbands for them? No, my daughters; it is far more bitter for me than for you, for the hand of the LORD has gone out against me."

14They lifted up their voices and wept again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her.

15She said, "See, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and to her gods. Return after your sister-in-law."

16But Ruth said, "Do not press me to leave you, to turn back from following you. For where you go, I will go, and where you lodge, I will lodge. Your people shall be my people, and your God my God.

17Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD do so to me and more also, if anything but death parts me from you."

18When she saw that she was determined to go with her, she stopped speaking to her.

Bethlehem

19So the two of them went on until they came to Bethlehem. And it came to pass, when they came to Bethlehem, that the whole town was stirred because of them, and the women said, "Is this Naomi?"

20She said to them, "Do not call me Naomi; call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.

21I went out full, and the LORD has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi, when the LORD has testified against me, and the Almighty has brought disaster on me?"

22So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, with her, who returned from the country of Moab. They came to Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.

Notes

  • v1 "in the days when the judges ruled" — bi-ymei shefot ha-shofetim, in the days of the judging of the judges. The book is set in the time of Judges and follows it in the canon; it ends with the name of David (4:17, 22). Bethlehem is house of bread, and the story begins with a famine there.

  • v1 "to live as a guest" — lagur, the verb of the ger. An Israelite family becomes the guests in Moab; the Moabite woman will become the guest in Israel.

  • v2 "Elimelech… Naomi… Mahlon and Chilion" — Elimelekh is my God is king, a name in a book that follows there was no king in Israel (Judges 21:25). Naomi is pleasant, the name she refuses in v20. Ephrathites: Ephrath is an old name of Bethlehem (Genesis 35:19).

  • v4 "Moabite wives" — Deuteronomy 23:3 says No Ammonite or Moabite shall enter the assembly of the LORD. The book tells, without arguing, how a Moabite woman came into the line of David.

  • v6 "the LORD had visited His people" — paqad, the verb of Joseph's promise, God will surely visit you (Genesis 50:24). The LORD acts in the book twice by the narrator's word: here, and when He gives Ruth conception (4:13).

  • v8 "loyal love" — chesed, the book's key word. Naomi asks the LORD to show it to the Moabite women who have shown it to her family; it returns at 2:20 and 3:10.

  • v14 "Ruth clung to her" — davqah, the verb of Genesis 2:24, a man leaves his father and his mother and clings to his woman. Ruth leaves her mother's house (v8) and clings to her mother-in-law.

  • vv16–17 "Your people shall be my people, and your God my God" — Ruth swears by the LORD, the God of Israel, not the gods of Moab to which Orpah returned (v15). May the LORD do so to me and more also is the form of a solemn oath.

  • v20 "call me Mara" — Mara, bitter, against Naomi, pleasant. The Almighty, Shaddai, as in Numbers 24:4. She uses the old name for God twice, with the LORD twice between.

  • v21 "the LORD has testified against me" — anah vi, answered against me, the phrase for a witness in court. The Greek has the Lord has humbled me, reading the same letters from another root.

chapters.title: Ruth in the Field of Boaz
chapters.html:
Ruth 2

Gleaning

1Naomi had a relative of her husband's, a man of worth, of the clan of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz.

2Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Let me go to the field and glean among the ears of grain after someone in whose eyes I may find favor." She said to her, "Go, my daughter."

3So she went and came and gleaned in the field after the reapers, and as it happened, she came to the part of the field belonging to Boaz, who was of the clan of Elimelech.

4Just then Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to the reapers, "The LORD be with you." They said to him, "The LORD bless you."

5Boaz said to his young man who was in charge of the reapers, "Whose young woman is this?"

6The young man in charge of the reapers answered, "She is the Moabite young woman who came back with Naomi from the country of Moab.

7She said, 'Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves after the reapers.' So she came, and she has stood from the morning until now; she has sat in the house only a little."

Boaz and Ruth

8Boaz said to Ruth, "Listen, my daughter. Do not go to glean in another field, and do not leave this one, but keep close to my young women.

9Keep your eyes on the field they are reaping, and go after them. Have I not commanded the young men not to touch you? When you are thirsty, go to the vessels and drink what the young men have drawn."

10She fell on her face, bowed down to the ground and said to him, "Why have I found favor in your eyes, that you should take notice of me, when I am a foreigner?"

11Boaz answered her, "All that you have done for your mother-in-law since your husband's death has been fully told to me: how you left your father and your mother and the land of your birth, and came to a people you did not know before.

12May the LORD repay your work, and may your reward be full from the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge."

13She said, "May I find favor in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me and spoken to the heart of your servant, though I am not like one of your servants."

14At mealtime Boaz said to her, "Come here and eat some of the bread, and dip your piece in the vinegar." So she sat beside the reapers, and he passed her roasted grain, and she ate and was satisfied and had some left over.

15When she rose to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, "Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not shame her.

16Also pull out some for her from the bundles and leave it for her to glean, and do not rebuke her."

17So she gleaned in the field until evening. Then she beat out what she had gleaned, and it was about an ephah of barley.

The Redeemer

18She took it up and went into the town, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. She also brought out and gave her what she had left over after being satisfied.

19Her mother-in-law said to her, "Where did you glean today? Where have you worked? Blessed be the man who took notice of you." So she told her mother-in-law with whom she had worked, and said, "The name of the man with whom I worked today is Boaz."

20Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, "Blessed be he by the LORD, whose loyal love has not forsaken the living or the dead." Naomi also said to her, "The man is a close relative of ours; he is one of our redeemers."

21Ruth the Moabite said, "He also said to me, 'Keep close to my young men until they have finished all my harvest.'"

22Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, "It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, so that you are not harmed in another field."

23So she kept close to the young women of Boaz, gleaning until the end of the barley harvest and the wheat harvest. She lived with her mother-in-law.

Notes

  • v1 "a man of worth" — ish gibbor chayil, the phrase used of Gideon (Judges 6:12) and Jephthah (11:1), there a mighty man of valor. Chayil is strength, wealth and worth together; here it is a landowner's standing. Boaz will call Ruth eshet chayil, a woman of worth (3:11), the same word. The written text has meyudda, the reading moda, a relative; the meaning is the same.

  • v2 "glean among the ears of grain" — the law left the edges of the field and the fallen grain for the poor and for the guest (Leviticus 19:9–10). Ruth, a foreigner and a widow, claims it.

  • v3 "as it happened" — va-yiqer miqreha, her chance chanced. The narrator calls it chance; Naomi will call it the LORD's loyal love (v20).

  • v7 "she has sat in the house only a little" — the Hebrew is hard to follow here, and the house may be a shelter in the field. The Greek reads she did not rest in the field even a little.

  • v10 "take notice of me, when I am a foreigner" — le-hakkireni… nokhriyyah, two words from the same root, nkr: to recognize and to be a stranger. Why would he know her, when she is unknown?

  • v11 "you left your father and your mother and the land of your birth" — the call of Abram in Genesis 12:1, from your land, and from your kindred, and from your father's house. Ruth did it with no promise.

  • v12 "under whose wings you have come to take refuge" — kenafav. In 3:9 Ruth asks Boaz to spread his kanaf, the wing or edge of his garment, over her. He prays for the LORD's wing; she asks for his.

  • v13 "spoken to the heart of your servant" — the phrase of Genesis 34:3 and 50:21 for speaking kindly. Your servant is shifchatekha; at 3:9, on the threshing floor, she uses the other word for a woman servant, amatekha.

  • v20 "whose loyal love has not forsaken the living or the dead" — the Hebrew can be read of the LORD or of Boaz. The blessing asks the LORD to bless Boaz, and the loyal love may be either's; the Greek reads it the same way. One of our redeemers, go'alenu: the go'el is the nearest relative, who buys back a family's land (Leviticus 25:25).

  • v23 "until the end of the barley harvest and the wheat harvest" — the barley harvest begins the count of seven full sabbaths that ends with the new grain offering of the wheat (Leviticus 23:15–16). Ruth gleans for the whole of it.

chapters.title: The Threshing Floor
chapters.html:
Ruth 3

Naomi's Plan

1Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, "My daughter, should I not seek rest for you, so that it may be well with you?

2And now, is not Boaz our relative, whose young women you have been with? Tonight he is winnowing barley at the threshing floor.

3Wash and anoint yourself, put on your clothes and go down to the threshing floor. But do not make yourself known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.

4When he lies down, note the place where he lies. Then go in, uncover his feet and lie down, and he will tell you what to do."

5She said to her, "All that you say I will do."

At Midnight

6She went down to the threshing floor and did all that her mother-in-law had commanded her.

7When Boaz had eaten and drunk, and his heart was merry, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. Then she came quietly, uncovered his feet and lay down.

8And it came to pass at midnight that the man was startled and turned over, and there was a woman lying at his feet.

9He said, "Who are you?" She said, "I am Ruth your servant. Spread your wing over your servant, for you are a redeemer."

10He said, "May you be blessed by the LORD, my daughter. You have made this last loyal love greater than the first, in not going after young men, whether poor or rich.

11And now, my daughter, do not be afraid. All that you say I will do for you, for all the people at the gate of my town know that you are a woman of worth.

12And now, it is true that I am a redeemer, but there is a redeemer nearer than I.

13Stay here tonight. And it shall come to pass in the morning, if he will redeem you, good, let him redeem. But if he is not willing to redeem you, then as the LORD lives, I will redeem you myself. Lie down until the morning."

14So she lay at his feet until the morning, and rose before one could recognize another. He said, "Let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor."

15He said, "Bring the cloak you are wearing and hold it out." She held it, and he measured out six measures of barley and put it on her. Then he went into the town.

Naomi Waits

16She came to her mother-in-law, who said, "How did it go, my daughter?" She told her all that the man had done for her,

17and said, "He gave me these six measures of barley, for he said, 'Do not go back empty to your mother-in-law.'"

18She said, "Wait, my daughter, until you know how the matter turns out, for the man will not rest until he has settled it today."

Notes

  • v1 "rest for you" — manoach, the word Naomi prayed in 1:9: May the LORD grant that you find rest, each of you in the house of her husband. What she asked the LORD for, she now sets out to arrange.

  • vv4, 7, 8, 14 "his feet" — margelotav, the place of his feet, found in this chapter and once in Daniel. Feet can be a polite word for what is not named (Judges 3:24, covering his feet), and the chapter never says more than feet. What happens at night is left as the text leaves it.

  • v9 "Spread your wing over your servant" — kenafekha, the wing or corner of a garment. Boaz had prayed that she would find refuge under the LORD's wings (2:12); she asks him to be the answer. To spread the corner of one's garment over a woman is a sign of taking her in marriage: God says it of Jerusalem, I spread My wing over you… and entered into a covenant with you (Ezekiel 16:8), and Deuteronomy 22:30 forbids uncovering a father's wing, his wife.

  • v9 "for you are a redeemer" — the go'el buys back a family's land (Leviticus 25:25). Ruth joins the duty of the redeemer to the duty of marrying a dead man's widow (Deuteronomy 25:5), which the law gives to a brother, not a redeemer. Chapter 4 holds the two together.

  • v10 "this last loyal love greater than the first" — the first was to Naomi (1:8, 2:11); the last is to the family's dead, in seeking a husband who can raise up a name for Mahlon (4:10).

  • v11 "a woman of worth" — eshet chayil, as Boaz is a man of worth (2:1). The same two words open the poem of Proverbs 31:10, A woman of worth, who can find? All the people at the gate is all the gate of my people, the town's gathering place and law court, where chapter 4 is set.

  • v12 "a redeemer nearer than I" — the story's one obstacle, named at the moment it seems solved. The written text has an extra im here that is not read.

  • v14 "before one could recognize another" — yakkir, the verb of 2:10, that you should take notice of me.

  • v15 "six measures of barley" — the measure is not named. Six of anything would be a heavy load for one woman, and the Hebrew gives no unit.

  • v17 "Do not go back empty" — reqam, the word of Naomi's lament: the LORD has brought me back empty (1:21). Boaz's words are not reported in vv14–15; Ruth reports them here, in words that answer Naomi.
